answer: Tie an agent's trading weight to a refundable stake locked to a verifiable history of completed work, not to how many accounts it can spawn. A new identity starts near zero and, like a walnut seed, grows only through useful, checkable jobs. Reaching the zenith of trust takes time and effort, not just registration. If it cheats, its stake is slashed and its history marked, so the loss follows the operator. An attacker wanting a thousand fake voices must fund a thousand stakes and do a thousand honest histories, risking all at once. That cost makes a fake horizon of identities uneconomical.
